title: Multiple invariants
concept: Multiple invariants on a type compose independent validation checks — each one verified separately, all must hold simultaneously.
why: Breaking complex validation into multiple simple invariants makes violations easier to debug and the code easier to maintain.
theory:
## Composing Multiple Invariants

```xiom
pub type Username = Str
  invariant: this.len() >= 3;
  invariant: this.len() <= 20;
  invariant: this.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii());
  invariant: !this.contains(" ");
  invariant: this.chars().next().is_alphabetic();
```

### Why Multiple Simple > One Complex

```xiom
// Hard to debug — which part failed?
pub type Username = Str
  invariant: this.len() >= 3 && this.len() <= 20 &&
             this.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii()) &&
             !this.contains(" ");

// Easy to debug — each check reports independently
pub type Username = Str
  invariant: this.len() >= 3;            // "username too short"
  invariant: this.len() <= 20;           // "username too long"
  invariant: this.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii());  // "non-ASCII chars"
  invariant: !this.contains(" ");        // "spaces not allowed"
```

### Order Matters for Performance

```xiom
pub type FilePath = Str
  invariant: this.len() < 4096;          // Cheap: O(1)
  invariant: this.chars().all(|c| c != 0); // Medium: O(n)
  invariant: !this.contains("..");       // Medium: O(n)
```

### Checked Independently
Each invariant is a separate runtime check. A violation in invariant #3 doesn't prevent #4 from being checked (in debug mode with full reporting).
tips: Break complex validation into focused, single-responsibility invariants
Place cheap checks (length, nullity) before expensive checks (scanning, allocation)
Each invariant gets its own error message — making debugging much faster
If two invariants overlap, consider combining them to avoid redundant checks
common_mistakes: Creating a single mega-invariant — hard to tell which part failed
Writing overlapping invariants that check the same thing twice
Ordering expensive invariants before cheap ones — wasteful when the cheap one fails
